reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E4) only addresses room-temperature or mild-temperature (20–60 °C) passivation and corrosion; none of it provides data on film behavior, phase transformations, or cracking at 700–900 °C. The key high-temperature premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Pre-exposed Q235 steel has a dense, adherent passivation film that is protective at room temperature.
At 700–900 °C, this film thermally decomposes and undergoes phase transformation to non-protective oxides.
Thermal expansion mismatch causes microcracking and spallation of the film at high temperature.
Film degradation allows rapid chloride ingress and accelerated substrate corrosion.
